name: Age of Empires IV
steal: D's direct model: one 60px resource bar, one bottom deck (minimap · command grid · queue · inspector), left panel only on demand. Resources read as a single scan line.
picks: Village fight — selection bottom-left, minimap bottom-right
Town at rest — resource bar and deck

name: Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition
steal: The canonical deck geometry: minimap bottom-left, command card bottom-centre, selection bottom-right. Idle-villager and age-up affordances never move.
picks: Desert town — deck with right-side selection

name: Age of Mythology: Retold
steal: Same skeleton as AoE2, but god powers and myth units get bigger, more legible tiles. Shows how 12 command tiles can read as abilities, not buttons.
picks: Naval fight — top bar and deck

name: Company of Heroes 3
steal: Tactical map top-left, VP/resource ticker top-right, unit cards bottom-centre with veterancy pips. Almost no chrome over the battlefield; the HUD hugs the edges.
picks: Desert fight — tactical map, unit cards
Winter fight — vet pips and abilities
Snow fight — tactical map + unit cards

name: Total War: WARHAMMER III
steal: Campaign and battle use different HUDs. Battle puts unit cards bottom, selected unit right, minimap bottom-right. Heavy ornament, always outside the play area.
picks: Campaign map — army and settlement panels
Battle — unit cards, minimap, selected unit

name: Manor Lords
steal: Diegetic and almost HUD-less. Building and people panels slide in from the right; approval, treasury and population are small top-left tokens. Sim depth lives in panels, not rails.
picks: Build menu — bottom bar and placement

name: Anno 1800
steal: Bottom-centre build menu with a category ring, minimap bottom-left, goods in a top ribbon. Dense production chains stay in one horizontal band.

name: Frostpunk 2
steal: City vitals top-left, heat/timeline bottom, faction council left. Stark monochrome plus one accent; the HUD reads as a diegetic instrument panel.
picks: City map — top bar and district markers
City — resource bar and district UI
Research — tech tree and detail panel

name: Against the Storm
steal: Best modern run-based city-builder HUD: resource strip on top, settlement panel left, orders/glades right, build bar bottom. Every corner has exactly one job.
picks: Grid city — build bar and orders

name: Northgard
steal: Compact, console-friendly HUD: clan vitals top-left, objectives top-right, minimap bottom-left, selection bottom-right. Very little screen coverage.

name: They Are Billions
steal: Survival-RTS HUD: colony stats top-left, wave timer top-centre, build grid bottom-centre, minimap bottom-left. Threat is the loudest element on screen.

name: Warcraft III: Reforged
steal: Hero-centric deck: hero portrait and inventory bottom-left, command card bottom-right, unit cards centre. Shows how one unit can own a whole panel.
picks: Battle — unit cards and hero panel

name: Total War: THREE KINGDOMS
steal: Character-first campaign UI: portraits, relationships and retinues in a right rail; battle deployment is a full-screen board. Good model for the People and Victory tabs.

name: Victoria 3
steal: The definitive Pop and macro-economics HUD: state capacities and balance deltas in top bar, left lens system (Production, Politics, Diplomacy, Military), Pop strata (Lower, Middle, Upper) with Standard of Living, radical/loyalist split, and market goods pricing.
picks: Buildings & production methods — employment by strata, wages, weekly balance
Strategic map — left lens bar, top capacity indicators, outliner
Diplomatic and market trade — goods supply/demand and trade routes

name: Crusader Kings III
steal: Character-first RPG strategy HUD: bottom-left character window with 3D portrait, traits, stress, health and opinions; top-left realm & council management; right-rail outliner; character interaction ring.
picks: Character sheet — traits, stress, lifestyle, relationships and claims
Council & realm window — minister appointments and active tasks
Campaign map — character anchor, realm currencies, situational alerts
